$comment: include-component-in-tag false gives plain v0.1.0 tags, which is what publish.yml matches on and what the community pieces use. There is deliberately no extra-files entry for the root package-lock.json: extra-files paths resolve inside the package directory, so '../../package-lock.json' made every run abort with 'illegal pathing characters in path'. The mismatch it was guarding against is harmless anyway. A workspace member's version field is not a dependency constraint, so npm ci ignores it. Verified on the v0.1.2 tag, which carried package.json 0.1.2 against a lock recording 0.1.1: publish.yml ran npm install -g npm@latest then npm ci and passed.
